title: feat(sdui-parser): diagnose the inert quickAdd on the ObjectKanban tags instead of calling it unknown
body:
Refs #8285 — **slice C only**. The card stays **open** after this lands: it then blocks on the `@objectstack/spec` retirement card, per the ruling's Execution paragraph. Deliberately not `Fixes`.

`Clause-②: yes` — four new exported symbols on a published package (`checkKanbanQuickAdd`, `INERT_QUICK_ADD`, `QUICK_ADD_HOST_TYPES`, `QUICK_ADD_KEY` from `@object-ui/sdui-parser`), and the already-published `Diagnostic` runtime payload gains a new `code` value, `inert-quick-add`, which consumers switch on. Under the mechanical floor either half alone is `yes`.

## What is ruled, and what this implements

The director-seat ruling on #8285 (comment 5583979207, decision batch #91) answered the A/B half — **B**: `quickAdd` retires from `object-kanban` / `kanban` and stays on `kanban-ui`, where a React host can supply the function. This PR is the interim the ruling names verbatim:

> **C now:** until the pin moves, `quickAdd: true` with no `onQuickAdd` is diagnosed at the html tier instead of dropped.

## ⚠️ Premise correction — the tier was not silent, it was WRONG

Re-measured on this branch's base `4fa0eb9c4`, by predicate rather than by copying the card's anchors.

The card was filed saying the key is dropped "with no diagnostic". That is true of the **spec** validator, which accepts it, and **false of the html tier**: `quickAdd` is deliberately absent from `OBJECT_KANBAN_INPUTS` (objectui#8201 escalated it rather than declaring it), so `validateTree` already reported it — as `unknown-prop`, "has no prop quickAdd".

That message is a **misdiagnosis**, which is why slice C still has content. `@objectstack/spec`'s `ComponentPropsMap['object-kanban']` publishes `quickAdd`, so an author who checks the contract finds the warning contradicted, concludes the manifest is behind the spec, and keeps a key that will never do anything. It is also indistinguishable from a typo, so nothing records *why* the key is refused. objectui#8201's own pin header measured this shape from the other direction: a tier that calls a working spelling unknown "trains authors (AI authors included) to delete working metadata".

The defect itself is intact and was re-measured, not inherited: `onQuickAdd` appears **0** times in `packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx`, against **6** for the control `onCardClick` in the same file, so the zero is a reading. The Quick Add control is gated on both halves (`quickAdd && onQuickAdd`) and `onQuickAdd` is an objectui#6124 runtime slot — a function. On this tier the second half is not merely absent but unwritable: a handler attribute on a parsed page draws `forbidden-attr` (measured). So there is no out-of-band consumer to protect, which is what makes this diagnostic unconditional rather than escape-hatched the way `unconsumed-widget-option` is.

## The change

`packages/sdui-parser/src/kanban-quick-add.ts` — a new module in the shape of the objectui#5709 precedent next door. `validateTree` asks it once per authored prop, **ahead of** the declaration lookup, and its answer **replaces** what the walk would otherwise say about the key rather than joining it (two diagnostics for one mistake is what `checkMemberTypes` already refuses, objectui#8067). Asked ahead of the lookup on purpose: the claim is about the render path, so a later decision to declare the key must not silently disarm the warning.

The message names the missing half of the pair and points at `kanban-ui`, where the pair works.

**Severity: warning — the escalation is deliberately not taken.** The ruling's word is "diagnosed", not "refused". `unknown-prop`, what this replaces, was already a warning, so nothing hardens: `compile()` still returns `ok` and no page that saves today stops saving. `validate.ts`'s own `inert-expression` note records that escalating an inert authored key to `error` is a separate question (objectui#6614 Q2) belonging at the save gate, and objectui#5709's ruling constrains this family directly — "no gate weakening and no new red gates were ruled". The hardening belongs to the contract, and option B is exactly that.

**This diagnoses; it does not widen.** `quickAdd` is still undeclared on both registrations — a pinned row asserts it.

## Scope, kept as dispatched

- ⛔ No spec change — retiring `object-kanban.quickAdd` from `ComponentPropsMap` is the separate cross-repo card.
- ⛔ objectui does not stop forwarding `quickAdd` on the two `ObjectKanbanRenderer` tags — that follows the spec pin, not C.
- ⛔ No inline record-creation path (option A) — ruled against. No `dataSource.create`, no permissions / required-field / rollback work.
- ⛔ `kanban-ui` keeps the `quickAdd` / `onQuickAdd` pair untouched, and draws no new diagnostic. A pinned control asserts it.
- ⛔ objectui#8201 is not addressed here and remains open.
- A falsy `quickAdd` is untouched (the renderer gates on `quickAdd && onQuickAdd`, so it asked for no control and got none), and a braced value stays `inert-expression`'s subject.

**This module is scheduled for deletion** by the change that lands the spec pin. The live pin carries a tripwire row for that: it asserts the spec still publishes the key, so it reddens on the day the retirement lands.

## Ablation — the pin is red without the change and green with it

Mutation: the four-line dispatch removed from `validate.ts`; the marker `checkKanbanQuickAdd(node.type, key, value)` counted **1 → 0** on disk, blob `c956914` → `ee95db2`, so the edit is proven landed rather than assumed. Restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, proven by an empty `git diff HEAD`, a clean `git status`, and the blob hash back to `c956914`. `@object-ui/sdui-parser` is aliased to its `src` in `vitest.config.mts`, so both suites read the mutated source; no `dist` is involved on either leg.

| | rows | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Subjects** — red without the change | 9 | `object-kanban` / `kanban` × (draws exactly one `inert-quick-add` warning · it REPLACES the false `unknown-prop` · the message names the missing half and where the pair works); the whole-pipeline row from real source text; and both live-registry rows |
| **Controls** — green in BOTH worlds | 17 | each named in a source comment with the wrong fix it guards |

Every control names its wrong fix in a comment, per the discipline: the unknown-prop control (a fix that turned the generic walk off for the block rather than answering for the key); `kanban-ui` (a fix scoped to "a kanban-ish tag", which would hit the one block the ruling keeps); a falsy `quickAdd` (a fix keyed on the key's presence rather than the author's request); the braced marker (a fix that read the parser's opaque `$expr` object as truthy); `ok` staying true (the escalation to `error`); plus the tag-set derivation, the still-not-declared rows, the spec tripwire and the zero-`onQuickAdd` tripwire.

`26 passed` with the change; `9 failed | 17 passed` without it.

Its own census line reads `0 real, 0 wrong-path, 0 fabricated`, and 0 of its lines name `sdui-parser`. A build prerequisite, not a finding. |

**Declared narrowing:** the repo-wide `eslint .` run is CI's, not this PR's. The narrowing is a measurement, not a skip: the population is read from eslint's own config, the count from its `--format json` output, and **type-aware linting is not enabled** anywhere in `eslint.config.js` (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict of any file it does not touch.

## Documentation

`content/docs/plugins/plugin-kanban.mdx` gains a short prose section under Event Handling saying that Quick Add is a `kanban-ui` capability, why an object-driven board cannot have it, and what the new warning is — mirroring how the `unconsumed-widget-option` warning is documented on the dashboard page.

## Measured and NOT fixed

- `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`'s `'object-kanban.quickAdd'` ledger entry still says objectui#8201 owns the question and "its answer deletes this entry". Stale after batch #91 — the ruling moved the question here and answered it B. Left alone: a docs nit inside a test ledger, and it has a real successor, since the follow-up that stops forwarding the key must delete the entry anyway (the key leaves `ComponentPropsMap`).
- `kanban-ui` also draws `unknown-prop` for an authored `quickAdd`: its registration publishes three inputs (`columns`, `onCardMove`, `className`) while its schema face accepts many more. That is the objectui#8201 declaration-gap shape on a block nobody has censused — but only this one key was measured, and objectui#8201 is open and owns that family, so nothing is filed on one instance.
